candidates.original_title: Online programs improve relationship functioning for distressed low-income couples: Results from a nationwide randomized controlled trial
candidates.description: OurRelationship program produces reliable improvements in relationship functioning relative to a 6-month waitlist control group for low-income couples seeking help
candidates.citation_sentence: In the current study, we report on a subset of these couples- those whose treatment assignments replicated those in Doss et al. (2020).

candidates.original_title: Online programs improve relationship functioning for distressed low-income couples: Results from a nationwide randomized controlled trial
candidates.description: OurRelationship program produces greater reductions in communication conflict than ePREP program for low-income couples seeking help
candidates.citation_sentence: In the current study, we report on a subset of these couples- those whose treatment assignments replicated those in Doss et al. (2020).
candidates.notes: Frequentist analysis shows no statistically reliable difference between programs on communication conflict, but Bayesian analysis provides evidence supporting the original differential effect. The 95% credible interval for the differential effect barely includes zero [-.348, .002].

candidates.original_title: Online programs improve relationship functioning for distressed low-income couples: Results from a nationwide randomized controlled trial
candidates.description: The OurRelationship and ePREP programs produce greater improvements in relationship satisfaction than a waitlist control group among low-income couples.
candidates.citation_sentence: Each of the during-intervention effect sizes reported in Doss and colleagues (2020) was reproduced (including IPV) in the current study with a single exception: During the treatment period, the OurRelationship program produced reliably smaller reductions in communication conflict compared to the waitlist control group in the current sample than in the previous sample (difference between current and previous study: d = 0.177; see Table 1).
candidates.notes: [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Online programs improve relationship functioning for distressed low-income couples: Results from a nationwide randomized controlled trial
candidates.description: The OurRelationship program produces a greater reduction in communication conflict than the ePREP program.
candidates.citation_sentence: This result is somewhat different than Doss and colleagues (2020) original study, which found that OurRelationship produced larger reductions in communication conflict than ePREP.
candidates.notes: The replication found no statistically reliable between-program difference, although Bayesian analyses indicated that the magnitude of the original difference was narrowly reproduced; the authors state that more research is needed.
